description: The line plot, titled “BBQ,” illustrates the relationship between model accuracy and the number of demonstrations for four different alignment methods: Squared Exponential, Tanh, ELU, and LLaMA-2-chat-7B. The x-axis, labeled “#Demonstrations,” spans from 0 to 1500 with linear spacing and tick marks at intervals of 250. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 45 to 60, also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The Squared Exponential method (dark blue line with circular markers) begins at approximately 53.5 accuracy at 0 demonstrations, rises steeply to about 57.5 at 250, and continues to climb gradually to roughly 59.5 at 1500. The Tanh method (medium blue line with circular markers) starts near 50, increases steadily to about 54.5 at 1500. The ELU method (light blue line with circular markers) begins at approximately 48, rises slowly to around 53.5 at 1500. The LLaMA-2-chat-7B baseline (pink dashed line with circular markers) remains nearly flat, starting at about 46.5 and ending at approximately 47.5, showing minimal improvement across the demonstration range.
